extracted.intended_audience: Members of the British Parliament, ministers, Company directors, and the politically engaged public concerned with East India Company colonial policy
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and normative standards for judging ministerial and Company conduct in administering conquered Indian territories (the Carnatic and Tanjore), including fiscal priorities, treatment of debts, infrastructure maintenance, transparency, and protection of native populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government must maintain the people before extracting revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: In order that the people, after a long period of vexation and plunder, may be in a condition to maintain government, government must begin by maintaining them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize relief and reconstruction expenditures so the population can recover fertility and population; revenue follows restoration, not vice versa. The road to economy in devastated countries lies through expense, not through immediate receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize restoration and public works (irrigation/reservoirs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Carnatic's prosperity depends on reservoirs and waterworks: these monuments of real kings must be reestablished and maintained at mighty charge or the country perishes irretrievably.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in repairing and maintaining irrigation infrastructure (reservoirs, watercourses, sluices). These public works are the 'national bank' and require perpetual credit; neglect leads to irreversible ruin of agriculture and revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce nonessential establishments and apply funds to revive unproductive regions
rubrics_metrics.description: A virtuous ministry would have reduced all their most necessary establishments; they would have suspended the justest payments; they would have employed every shilling derived from the producing to reanimate the powers of the unproductive parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cut or suspend routine/state expenditures when a territory is devastated and redirect available funds to immediate support and rehabilitation of productive capacity (plough as first creditor).

rubrics_metrics.name: First creditor of a country is agricultural production ('the plough')
rubrics_metrics.description: They would have proclaimed ... that on every country the first creditor is the plough -- that this original, indefeasible claim supersedes every other demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give priority to agricultural recovery over private creditors, interest payments, or ceremonial/state splendor; ensure food production and livelihoods before servicing debts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not convert war devastation into enforceable public debt of the people
rubrics_metrics.description: They are absurd enough to consolidate all the calamities of war into debts -- to metamorphose the devastations of the country into demands upon its future production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid accounting practices or policies that treat losses from invasion/war as debts owed by the conquered populace; do not charge devastated populations for the costs of wars they suffered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use accurate, recent, and full evidence for revenue estimates; do not suppress contrary reports
rubrics_metrics.description: To call ministers' reliance on an old speculative estimate as justification is wrong: they have wilfully and corruptly suppressed the information which they ought to have produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base fiscal charges and policy on up-to-date, authorized records (committee reports, actual receipts); disclose and consider committee findings rather than clinging to outdated speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not hand territories back to ruinous local management without protective conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: They have delivered over those very territories ... into the ruinous mismanagement of the Nabob of Arcot ... without condition, without arrangement, without stipulation of any sort for the natives of any rank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When restoring or assigning territorial control, insist on arrangements, stipulations, or guarantees that protect inhabitants, secure revenue for public purposes, and prevent immediate re-enslavement to abusive local rulers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protectors' promises (protection/compensation) must be backed by retained jurisdiction or real power
rubrics_metrics.description: They have thought proper to mock and outrage their misery by ordering them protection and compensation. From what power is this protection to be derived, and from what fund is this compensation to arise? The revenues are delivered over to their oppressor; the territorial jurisdiction ... is surrendered to the same iron hands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compensation or protection pledges are hollow unless the administering power retains the jurisdiction or resources necessary to enforce them; ensure enforceable mechanisms before promising redress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid preference to private claims over public defence and civil government
rubrics_metrics.description: They have given preference to those fictitious private debts over the standing defence and the standing government. It is there the public is robbed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public funds must prioritize army, civil administration, credit, and investment necessary for territorial defence and governance before satisfying private creditors or speculative claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject manufacturing or validating private usurious debts through public policy
rubrics_metrics.description: They order the Nabob ... to allot four hundred and eighty thousand pounds a year, as a fund for the debts ... For the punctual payment of this annuity, they order him to give soucar security. ... The majority ... will hear with astonishment that these soucars are no other than the creditors themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not create state-allocated annuities or security arrangements that institutionalize predatory interest, enable creditors to become their own securities, or permit extortionate compound interest to be charged against territorial revenues.

rubrics_metrics.name: If lending is necessary, use straightforward, non-usurious methods (Company credit or direct assignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you know that the Nabob must annually mortgage his territories ... why is not the assignment or mortgage made directly to the Company itself? ... Or why do they not take that assignment with such interest to themselves as they pay to others, that is, eight per cent?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer direct assignments to the responsible authority or lending at reasonable market rates (e.g., Company's 8%) rather than permitting third-party usurers to exact 24-48% compound interest; avoid intermediaries who profit at the people's expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not reward or provide for private servants' emolument at the expense of devastated populations
rubrics_metrics.description: They were providing, not supply for the establishments of its protection, but rewards for the authors of its ruin. ... they have compelled that miserable enslaved body to put their hands to an order for appropriating the enormous sum ... as a fund for the private emolument of his creatures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent ministerial self-dealing and the diversion of public revenue to enrich Company servants or favourites, especially when the local population is impoverished by war and mismanagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid rescinding effective local committees and leases that improve revenue and welfare
rubrics_metrics.description: If these hopes from the committee are rational, remember that the committee is no more. Your ministers ... have put a complete end to that committee. Their acts are rescinded; their leases are broken; their renters are dispersed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustain successful local governance reforms and leases that raise revenue legitimately and improve order rather than abolishing them for political or predatory ends which will destroy recovered gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent cycles of dispossession where farmers and cultivators are repeatedly exploited
rubrics_metrics.description: The usurious European assignee supersedes the Nabob's native farmer ... the remaining miserable last cultivator ... is lashed from oppressor to oppressor ... by a ravenous, because a short-lived succession of claimants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies must avoid enabling repeated seizure and re-assignment of revenue rights that lead to chronic oppression of cultivators; protect stable tenure and fair treatment of native agricultural classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not allow creation of compounded interest obligations on public revenues
rubrics_metrics.description: All this time they know that by having a debt subsisting without any interest, which is to be paid by contracting a debt on the highest interest, they manifestly render it necessary ... to give the private demand a preference to the public; ... an usury of twenty, twenty-four, thirty-six, and even eight-and-forty per cent, with compound interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibit or guard against policies that allow compound interest at extreme rates to accumulate on territorial revenues; such obligations will render revenues insufficient even in long peace and amount to effective confiscation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not passively accept speculative 'peace' revenue estimates as authoritative
rubrics_metrics.description: Lord Macartney's sketch is a matter of speculation; it supposes the country restored to its ancient prosperity. If, therefore, the ministers have gone wrong, they were not deceived by Lord Macartney: they were deceived by no man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between speculative, peace-time estimates and actual receipts; policies should not be founded on optimistic hypothetical restoration but on measured, verifiable current yields and realistic projections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject legal-accounting fictions that make a territory 'indebted' to its own estate
rubrics_metrics.description: The Carnatic owes a shilling to the Company ... It owes nothing to the Company, for this plain and simple reason: the territory charged with the debt is their own. To say that their revenues fall short, and owe them money, is to say they are in debt to themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid circular accounting where an administering power claims a debt against territorial revenues that belong to itself; such 'debt' is a fiction used to justify exactions and should not be treated as a valid public demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not create indefinite confiscation clauses tied to future Company wars
rubrics_metrics.description: In case the Company's servants should be again involved in war ... he is to be subjected to a new penalty ... the country is to remain under confiscation until all the debt which the Company shall think fit to incur in such war shall be discharged: that is to say, forever.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid contractual terms that allow perpetual confiscation of revenues as security for future, undefined Company liabilities; such terms institutionally dispossess the native polity permanently.
